title: ugkrishnamurti.in — U.G. Krishnamurti: The Revolutionary Spiritual Teacher (home)
description: Home page of the main living U.G. Krishnamurti site (page title 'U.G. Krishnamnamurti [sic] - The Revolutionary Spiritual Teacher'; also 'Un-Guru'). States that UG's teaching carries no copyright and that he founded no schools, ashrams or meditation centres; gives his death as 22 March 2007 aged 89 in Vallecrosia. Navigation (confirmed in search snippets): About UG (Life Background, Key Events, Valentine de Kerven); UG's Essence in Words (My Approach, My Swan Song, Books & PDFs, Quotes); UG Speaks (Essential Audios, Essential Videos, Talks with NIMHANS Doctors, Interviews with UG, Old Audios); Remembering UG (Reflections by Friends); Resources & Archive (Magazine Articles, Snapshots - Press Articles, Money Maxims, Books About UG). Live and indexed 2025-26.

title: Contact: ugkfriends@gmail.com
description: The only contact channel on the site: shown under 'Email', 'Contact us' and 'Follow us' on the Books & PDFs page and as 'Contact us' on the Interviews with UG page. No newsletter, mailing list or event calendar surfaced.

title: Who runs ugkrishnamurti.in — anonymous volunteer 'friends' (operator not named)
description: No individual or organisation is named as operator anywhere found (no footer credit, no 'built by' line surfaced in any snippet); the site presents itself as run by friends of UG and uses the ugkfriends@gmail.com address. Negative finding confirmed again in wave 5 (a dedicated operator search returned nothing). A WHOIS lookup would be the next step.

title: About UG / Life Background (biography; obituary account by Mukunda Rao)
description: Page title 'UGK - Life Background'. Biographical page: born 1918 (spelled 'Masulipatam') into a Telugu Brahmin family, raised in a religious household by a Theosophist grandfather; University of Madras studies 'gave him no answers'; met Ramana Maharshi at 21; married 1943, four children; died March 2007 in Italy. Includes Mukunda Rao's obituary account: UG fell and injured himself about seven weeks before his death, refused medical treatment, died 22 March 2007 at 2:30 pm aged 88/89 in the apartment built for him by friends Lucia, Anita and Giovanni in their villa at Vallecrosia, Italy; cremated next day (23 March, 2:45 pm) by Mahesh Bhatt without rituals. Page carries photographs.

title: Life & Background
description: Life-background sub-page. Gives birth at Masulipatnam 9 July 1918; the December 1953 encounter with J. Krishnamurti; and places the onset of 'the most astounding and almost incomprehensible mystical experiences' in Paris, April 1967, in his 49th year (only this site gives Paris/April).

title: Valentine de Kerven (page)
description: Page on Valentine de Kerven, the Swiss consulate translator who sheltered UG in Geneva in December 1963 (she was about 63), gave up her job to look after him, set him up in Saanen near Gstaad during the 'halcyon days' 1963-67, was moved permanently to Bangalore in September 1986 as Alzheimer's advanced, and died at Poornakutee, Bangalore, 20 January 1991.

title: My Approach
description: Navigation item under UG's Essence in Words (confirmed in the home-page menu). The page itself was not returned by any search, so URL is a pattern guess and content unverified. The nearest known text with this heading is K. Chandrasekhar's 'Stopped in Our Tracks' excerpt 'My Approach' ('I am not a thinker in the sense in which the word is used... My objective in carrying on the conversation is to silence them'), hosted on the WELL.

title: My Swan Song (text)
description: Full text of UG's final statement, dictated to Louis Brawley in mid-February 2007 and signed 'Vallecrosia, February 2007'. Opening: 'What I have found of and by myself is that all teachers religious, secular and those scientists and filthy doctors are wrong...'. The site's version closely matches the WELL transcription; the Medium '[Updated]' copy differs and contains inserted commentary. Thirteen quotes in the project quote-base cite this page.
